proof:
The isolated parallel speeds and the separator give $\int_F\Xi_z\,dS=0$. On $F$ its cap contribution is constant almost everywhere by assumption, so use the smooth representative supplied by its energy and covariance terms. Its tangential Hessian is the restriction to the facet tangent space of the positive semidefinite matrix
$$
\sum_i\eta_i\delta_i\left[
\frac{\mathbf1_{z=p_i}(N+1)}{E_i} P_i(X)^{-N-2}a_i a_i^{\mathsf T}
+\frac1M\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}u_{ij}^{\mathsf T}
\right].
$$
Thus the representative is convex. If it is nonaffine, Jensen at the centroid $g_F$ is strict: a supporting affine function there lies below it, and equality in the mean would make them equal on $F$ by continuity and positive relative volume on every relatively open interior subset. Therefore $\Xi_z(g_F)<0$.

The superlevel of the tent at $1-s$ is $g_F+s(F-g_F)$ for $0<s<1$. By layer cake, change of variables in the $(d-1)$-dimensional facet, and convexity,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_F T\Xi_z\,dS
&=\int_0^1s^{d-1}\int_F\Xi_z(g_F+s(X-g_F))\,dS(X)\,ds\\
&\le |F|\Xi_z(g_F)\int_0^1s^{d-1}(1-s)\,ds
=\frac{|F|\Xi_z(g_F)}{d(d+1)}<0 .
\end{aligned}
$$
The isolated speed $-T$ violates the separator. Hence the representative is affine, so its tangential Hessian is zero. For each tangential direction every summand in the displayed quadratic form is nonnegative, and $\delta_i,\rho_{ij}$ are positive. Each positive group's covectors therefore annihilate every tangent direction, as does its own energy covector if $z=p_i$. The existence of the three paths under the given isolation condition is the isolated-facet signed realization theorem. Two nonparallel covectors cannot both lie in the one-dimensional normal line.
statement: In the regular singleton response setting take $\eta_i\ge0$ summing to one. Assume the corresponding separator satisfies $\sum_z\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi_zv_z\,dS\le0$ for every admissible response of its actual signed cone. Suppose $d\ge2$ and one old polytopal fiber has a facet $F$ on which that cone contains the isolated inward speeds $1,-1,-T$, where $T$ is the unit-height centroid pyramid tent on $F$ and all three speeds vanish surface-almost everywhere off $F$. The two-direction forced-contact isolation condition is sufficient for these three paths to be actual. Suppose also that for every cap with $\eta_i\theta_{ij}>0$ its selector on $F$ is constant surface-almost everywhere. Then for every $\eta_i>0$ and every $j$, the continuous covector $u_{ij}$ annihilates the tangent space of $F$. The same holds for the own energy covector of any such group whose source is in that fiber. In particular no such separator exists if every available group has two nonparallel continuous covectors.
title: Uncut free facet forces parallel normals in a regular buffered dual
